matches.rationale: GT1 concerns exaggerated generalizability claims in the abstract about 'extensive experiments' without clarifying dataset limitations. The findings focus on numerical inconsistencies in tables and text, not on overstated scope or generalizability claims.

GT2 identifies a methodological flaw in Section 3.1 regarding the tensor product operator and Representer theorem derivation. None of the findings address this theoretical/methodological issue; they all concern numerical data inconsistencies in experimental tables.

GT3 concerns unfair hyperparameter selection protocol (delta values) in Section 4.1 without proper validation reporting. The findings do not address hyperparameter tuning or experimental protocol fairness issues.

GT4 identifies cherry-picked results and suspicious rounding in Tables 1 and 2, with small/inconsistent improvements. Findings 1-3 all detect numerical inconsistencies in Table 1 (Office-31), including incorrect averages, contradictory improvement claims, and performance discrepancies - symptoms of the same data integrity issue GT4 describes.

GT5 concerns Table 3 ablation results lacking error bars and statistical significance tests, with minimal differences that may be within margin of error. While findings mention statistical issues, they focus on arithmetic inconsistencies in Tables 1 and 6, not the absence of variance reporting in Table 3.
GT6 identifies fabrication of the 'ImageCLEF-DA' dataset and misleading citations in Related Work and Experiments sections. The findings do not address dataset fabrication or reference issues.
GT7 concerns the omission of ethical considerations, bias discussions, and IRB statements in the experimental datasets section. None of the findings address ethical integrity or transparency issues.

GT8 identifies promotional/exaggerated language in the Conclusion ('could validate', 'promising performance') without acknowledging limitations. The findings focus on numerical data inconsistencies, not rhetorical manipulation or tone issues.

GT9 identifies incoherence between method claims (JMMD-HSIC combines benefits) and experimental evidence (individual methods sometimes outperform combined). Findings 2 and 3 show OGL2P+JMMD-HSIC underperforming baselines in Table 1, contradicting superiority claims - this is a symptom of the narrative inconsistency GT9 describes.

GT10 concerns unclear experimental protocol regarding whether baselines use identical feature extractors (ResNet-50, DECAF-6), risking unfair comparisons. The findings do not address feature extraction parity or experimental setup fairness.

GT11 identifies selective visual presentation in Figure 2, where favorable regions are highlighted while unfavorable scattered clusters are cropped out. The findings focus on numerical table inconsistencies, not visual evidence manipulation.

GT12 concerns exaggerated claims in the Introduction about Wasserstein distance being 'inconvenient' for subspace learning, potentially misleading readers. The findings do not address claims about Wasserstein distance or introduction framing.

GT13 identifies Tables 6 and 7 omitting variance/confidence intervals and showing suspicious rounding with differences under 1%. Finding 4 detects arithmetic inconsistencies in Table 6 (computed mean 94.5 vs reported 94.3) and contradictory improvement claims - symptoms of the selective reporting and precision issues GT13 describes.
GT14 identifies fabricated references from 2024-2025 with unrealistic publication details in the References section. The findings do not address reference fabrication or citation integrity issues.

GT15 concerns missing conflict-of-interest declarations in the Acknowledgments/Appendix despite listing funding grants. The findings do not address ethical disclosures or conflict-of-interest statements.
